Expanded training and temporal context · 12 November 2026

Selected candidate improves same-match spell F1

Fresh test: Barcelona–Real Madrid, La Liga, 18 December 2019. Five training matches, PSG–Marseille validation. Both family checkpoints and the primary candidate were frozen before test labels were opened.

Selected family: context. Experimental recommendation: candidate. Production default unchanged: these partial H/A labels cannot validate full-match dead-ball behaviour.

Candidate is the validation-selected family. Test ablations cannot be used to replace it. Misses/false positives use IoU 0.5; possible merges are descriptive geometric overlaps. Compare models on this same match, not scores from earlier matches.

What changed

Inter–Juventus and Liverpool–Manchester City expand training from three matches to five. The data-only model retains instantaneous features. The context model adds surrounding tracking over ±0.48 and ±2 seconds and movement contrast. Neither rejected spell loss weighting nor a boundary head is reused. One-layer RNNs are trained from scratch, with dropout, L2, clipping and validation spell-F1 checkpoint selection.

Limits

  • Automatic partial H/A labels are not independent full-match ground truth.
  • Validation has been repeatedly reused.
  • Heldout teams have appeared in an earlier viewed test but not in this training pool.
  • Context is offline, uses future tracking, and can span unknown-label gaps without filling their labels.
  • Unknown labels split/censor spells; no dead-ball supervision.
  • A different match score is not a cross-experiment F1 gain; compare models only on this same test.
  • Test ablations are diagnostic and must not be used to change the validation-selected candidate.
  • One fresh match is limited evidence; no statistical-significance or 0.8–0.9 guarantee.
